newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-JODY HULL SCORES WITH 5 SECONDS IN OT AS PANTHERS BEAT STARS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-JODY HULL SCORES WITH 5 SECONDS IN OT AS PANTHERS BEAT STARS.

text.p: Jody Hull's shorthanded goal with five seconds left in overtime gave the Florida Panthers a 2-1 victory over the Dallas Stars Friday in a battle of division leaders.

Florida was killing a slashing penalty to Scott Mellanby when goaltender John Vanbiesbrouck cleared the puck off the boards. Bill Lindsay beat two Dallas players to the loose puck at the Stars' blue line and broke in on goalie Andy Moog.
Moog smothered Lindsay's shot as the two collided but Hull deposited the rebound into the empty net for his third goal of the season and second in as many games.
"Lindsay has great speed and I had nobody on me," Hull said. "And I figured I had the best shot at a rebound."
He added: "Anytime you can play a top team in the other conference as well as we did tonight, then we know we're really establishing ourselves."
The win ended Florida's 41-game regular-season overtime winless streak (0-10-31) stretching back to December 1993.
Dallas was held to one shot in the first period and went 0-for-7 on the power play. The Stars also had two goals disallowed.

"It was a helluva hockey game as it was a great effort by us from wire-to-wire. We had goals called back, which made the loss real difficult," said Dallas coach Ken Hitchcock. "It's difficult to play as well as we did and have those things happen to us."

Lindsay broke up a goaltending duel at 4:48 of the third period. Dallas defenceman Richard Matvichuk coughed up the puck at his own blue line and Lindsay redirected Radek Dvorak's shot for his fourth goal of the season.

Adams and the Stars finally got a goal that counted at 11:40 to make it 1-1. Pat Verbeek sent a backhanded pass from behind the net to the slot and Adams whipped a shot that beat Vanbiesbrouck to the glove side.
Florida, which leads the Atlantic Division, improved to an NHL-best 6-1-3 on the road.
"It was a real good win in a game played by two real good teams," said Panthers coach Doug MacLean.
Dallas, the Central Division leader, lost for just the second time in its last seven games.
At Colorado, Valeri Kamensky scored twice and Patrick Roy made 21 saves to extend his personal unbeaten streak to 12 games, leading the Avalanche to a 3-2 victory over the New York Islanders.
Stephane Yelle also tallied for the Avalanche, who are 6-0-2 in their last eight home games. Colorado, which leads the league with 34 points, is 11-1-3 in its last 15 games.
Roy is 10-0-2 in his last 12 games, allowing just 19 goals in that span.
The Islanders took a 2-1 lead on Claude Lapointe's breakaway goal at 4:32 of the second period, but Yelle tied it just 84 seconds later.
Brent Hughes also scored for the Islanders, who dropped to 1-4-3 in their last eight games.

In Hartford, the Pittsburgh Penguins captured their first road win of the season as Jaromir Jagr scored his league-leading 17th and 18th goals and Ken Wregget made 37 saves in a 7-1 romp over the Whalers.

Pittsburgh was the lone NHL team without a road win at 0-11-1. But the Penguins had little trouble against shaky goaltender Jason Muzzatti, scoring five times in the third period to end a four-game winless streak at Hartford.
The loss ended Hartford's five-game unbeaten streak and dropped the first-place Whalers to 7-3-1 at home.

In Calgary, Eric Daze, Sergei Krivokrasov and Ethan Moreau scored in a 4:38 span of the third period and Tony Amonte had two goals as the Chicago Blackhawks stopped an eight-game winless streak against the Flames with a 5-2 victory.
German Titov scored two second-period goals to give the Flames a 2-1 edge entering the third, but then it was all Chicago.
Chicago, which had been 0-4-1 in its previous five games, defeated Calgary for the first time since last February.
Theo Fleury had two assists for the Flames, who are 2-7-1 in their last 10 games, scoring only 21 goals in that span.
At New Jersey, Chris Simon had his second two-goal game in five days and Olaf Kolzig made 38 saves as the Washington Capitals ended a seven-game losing streak against the Devils with a 5-1 victory.
Peter Bondra added a goal and two assists for Washington, which broke a 10-game winless streak against the Devils (0-9-1) stretching back to April 1, 1994.
